vendors.name: Snowflake
vendors.tagline: Snowflake is a cloud data platform. It has built-in semantic views, Cortex AI agents and a managed MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: Semantic Views are GA schema-level objects. They contain metrics, dimensions, relationships, synonyms and verified queries. Cortex Agents and the managed MCP server read them.

metrics.n: The METRICS clause supports aggregate, derived, window and semi-additive metrics. Access modifiers are PUBLIC or PRIVATE.

dimensions.n: DIMENSIONS and FACTS support filters, sample values and enum flags. YAML adds time_dimensions. The spec has no hierarchy construct.

relationships.n: RELATIONSHIPS support primary keys, many-to-one, one-to-one, ASOF and bridge tables. The USING relationship path and range joins are Preview.

synonyms.n: Synonyms use WITH SYNONYMS, COMMENT, SAMPLE_VALUES and IS_ENUM. Free-text instructions use AI_SQL_GENERATION and AI_QUESTION_CATEGORIZATION.

verifiedQueries.n: AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES are stored in the semantic view. A Verified Query Repository also exists. Optimization from verified queries is Preview.

nl2sql.n: Tools: Cortex Analyst API, Cortex Agents, CoWork. Since Aug 2026, Snowflake recommends Cortex Agents over standalone Cortex Analyst.

ontology.n: There is no object, link or action layer. Semantic views cover tables, relationships and metrics. Ossie has an Ontology working group.

graph.n: The SQL command and function indexes show no graph query feature. Partner apps are Neo4j Graph Analytics and RelationalAI.

vector.n: The VECTOR type is GA since May 2024. Cortex Search (vector plus keyword) is GA since Oct 2024. Dimensions can bind a Search service.

mcp.n: The managed MCP server is GA since Nov 2025. Tools: Cortex Analyst on a semantic view, Search, Agents, SQL and custom. The limit is 50 tools.

governance.n: RBAC grants, tags, ACCOUNT_USAGE views and agent lineage apply. Masking and row access policies apply at query time. The verified_by field is free text.

openStandard.n: Ossie (formerly OSI) YAML import and export is Preview since Jun 2026. Native YAML, GET_DDL, a dbt package and Terraform also exist.

offers: Semantic Views are schema-level objects. They have logical tables, relationships, facts, dimensions, metrics and synonyms. Agents read them as context.
Verified queries and text instructions live inside the semantic view. They follow its grants and shares.
Cortex Agents and CoWork generate SQL directly from semantic views. They run the SQL under Snowflake roles.
The managed MCP server exposes semantic views, Cortex Search, agents and SQL execution to external MCP clients. It uses RBAC.
Autopilot drafts a semantic view from tables, query history, example SQL, Power BI files or Tableau files.
Plain SQL queries on semantic views work from any SQL client. They use the SEMANTIC_VIEW clause or AGG.
gaps: There is no ontology layer (objects, links, actions). There is no native graph query. Graph work needs a partner Native App.
Semantic views live inside Snowflake. A metric layer shared with other warehouses needs an external tool.
The Ossie spec is pre-1.0. Release 0.1.1 is out and 0.2.0 is a draft. Snowflake import and export is Preview.
Several parts are Preview: relationship paths, range joins, materializations, TDS export, Horizon Context and verified-query optimization.
Names and entry points changed in 2026: Intelligence became CoWork and Analyst became Agents. Older tutorials and response formats do not match.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model the data as a semantic view with synonyms, sample values, verified queries and instructions. Add the view as a tool on a Cortex Agent. Call the agent through the Agents Run API, CoWork or the managed MCP server. Use Autopilot or Semantic Studio to draft the view. Keep the definition in Git through dbt or Terraform.

snippet.title: Minimal CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW over TPC-H sample data, adapted from the official example
snippet.code:
CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW tpch_rev_analysis
  TABLES (
    orders AS SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.TPCH_SF1.ORDERS PRIMARY KEY (o_orderkey) WITH SYNONYMS ('sales orders'),
    customers AS SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.TPCH_SF1.CUSTOMER PRIMARY KEY (c_custkey)
  )
  RELATIONSHIPS ( orders_to_customers AS orders (o_custkey) REFERENCES customers )
  DIMENSIONS (
    customers.customer_name AS customers.c_name WITH SYNONYMS = ('customer name'),
    orders.order_year AS YEAR(o_orderdate) COMMENT = 'Year when the order was placed'
  )
  METRICS (
    orders.order_average_value AS AVG(orders.o_totalprice) COMMENT = 'Average order value across all orders'
  )
  COMMENT = 'Semantic view for revenue analysis';

notes.topic: OSI: who started it and when
notes.text: Snowflake announced Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) on 2025-09-23. OSI is an open source initiative for a vendor-neutral semantic model spec. Snowflake leads it. The press release names Salesforce (with Tableau), BlackRock, dbt Labs and RelationalAI as launch partners.

sources.t: Snowflake press release: Open Semantic Interchange Initiative

notes.text: The Sep 2025 coalition also listed Alation, Atlan, Blue Yonder, Cube, Elementum AI, Hex, Honeydew, Mistral AI, Omni, Select Star, Sigma and ThoughtSpot. The Snowflake Jul 2026 post says 17 launch partners. It does not name them. It now counts more than 50 organizations. The press release does not use the term founding members.

sources.t: Snowflake press release: Open Semantic Interchange Initiative

notes.text: Nov 2025 additions: AWS, Collibra, DataHub, Domo, Firebolt, Informatica, Instacart, JPMC, Preset, Starburst Data, Strategy. Jan 2026 additions: AtScale, Coalesce, Collate, Credible, Databricks, JetBrains, Lightdash, Qlik. Denodo joined in Mar 2026. Kyvos joined in Aug 2026.

sources.t: Snowflake blog: OSI initiative expands partners (2025-11-13)

notes.topic: OSI spec status, version and license in 2026
notes.text: The spec is under Apache License 2.0. The spec file lists release 0.1.1 dated 2025-12-11. Snowflake announced the first version on 2026-01-27. On 2026-10-24 the main branch shows 0.2.0.dev0, marked draft and unreleased. The only git tag is osi-0.1.1-rc1. A v1.0 target was named in Nov 2025 with no date.

sources.t: Snowflake blog: OSI initiative expands partners

notes.text: Open Semantic Interchange entered the Apache Incubator on 2026-06-22. It was renamed Apache Ossie (incubating) to avoid confusion with the Open Source Initiative acronym. The Snowflake blog announced the rename on 2026-07-08. ossie.apache.org announced it on 2026-07-10. Spec, community and mission are unchanged. The code lives at github.com/apache/ossie. The ASF notes that incubation does not mean the code is complete or stable.

sources.t: Apache Ossie enters the Apache Incubator
dbt Labs: OSI is now Apache Ossie

notes.topic: Snowflake support for Ossie and OSI YAML
notes.text: Snowflake documents SYSTEM$CREATE_SEMANTIC_VIEW_FROM_OSSIE_YAML and SYSTEM$READ_OSSIE_YAML_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW. Snowflake-only features stay in vendor extensions. The older OSI-named procedure is marked deprecated. The Preview features list shows OSI YAML for semantic views as Preview since Jun 2026. The docs example uses spec version 0.1.1.

notes.topic: Product rename: Snowflake Intelligence to Snowflake CoWork
notes.text: Snowflake Intelligence became Snowflake CoWork. Cortex Code became CoCo. Snowflake announced both changes at Snowflake Summit on 2026-06-02. Current Snowflake docs use the CoWork and CoCo names. The 2025 GA release note for Snowflake Intelligence now points to the CoWork overview.

sources.t: Snowflake press release: Snowflake CoWork (formerly Snowflake Intelligence), 2026-06-02

notes.topic: Is the semantic model YAML file path legacy?
notes.text: Yes for the stage file. Snowflake calls stage-based semantic model YAML the legacy stage API. It still works with Cortex Analyst. Snowflake recommends semantic views for new work. Stage files lack SQL querying and native sharing. YAML is still a valid way to author a semantic view through SYSTEM$CREATE_SEMANTIC_VIEW_FROM_YAML and Semantic Studio.

notes.text: On 2026-08-28 Snowflake recommended moving from Cortex Analyst to Cortex Agents. The Cortex Analyst REST API stays available. Since 2026-04-13 agents generate SQL directly from semantic views. The response block type changed from cortex_analyst_text_to_sql to system_execute_sql.

notes.text: Semantic views entered Preview on 2025-04-17. Defining them became GA at Summit in June 2025. Querying them became GA in Aug 2025. Standard SQL clauses on semantic views became GA on 2026-03-02. Semantic Studio became GA on 2026-09-30. Cortex Agents and the managed MCP server became GA on 2025-11-04. Preview items: USING relationship paths, range joins, materializations, TDS export and Horizon Context (2026-10-12).

sources.t: Mar 2 2026 release note: standard SQL clauses GA
Sep 30 2026 release note: Semantic Studio GA
Managed MCP server GA release note

notes.text: A semantic view is a schema-level object. As with standard views, you grant SELECT on the view and need no SELECT on its base tables. Snowflake docs say the query engine enforces masking and row access policies when agents query data. Tags work on semantic views and their members since May 2026. Lineage links the table, semantic view and agent since Sep 2026.

Sep 2026 release note: lineage for Cortex Agents

notes.topic: BI tool support for semantic views
notes.text: Inbound: Autopilot builds a semantic view from a Power BI file (GA 2026-08-18) or a Tableau file. DAX measures become metrics. Outbound: SYSTEM$EXPORT_TDS_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW makes a Tableau data source (Preview, Mar 2026). Native semantic view support inside other BI tools is unverified.

sources.t: Power BI ingestion GA release note

notes.text: The Snowflake SQL command and function indexes show no property graph, SQL/PGQ or Cypher feature. Neo4j documents Graph Analytics for Snowflake (graph algorithms on Snowpark Container Services). RelationalAI lists a Snowflake Native App with graph reasoning.

Horizon Catalog is the catalog layer for descriptions, tags, lineage and access control. Horizon Context (Preview, 2026-10-12) adds metadata connectors to 18 external sources such as Power BI, Tableau, dbt, Databricks and BigQuery. The connectors read metadata from external systems.

Semantic View Autopilot has no Preview label in the docs. Power BI ingestion for it is GA. The docs list no GA release note for it. Flexera (third party) says GA since Feb 2026. These items are unverified: Tableau ingestion status, the exact GA date of Cortex Analyst (Preview Aug 2024), and third-party BI tools that read semantic views.
